## Maintainer ruling recorded — Option A: immediate retirement, no transition window — and a STANDING class rule

Provenance: maintainer, 2026-08-27, PM chat decision-inbox batch 6 (adjudication session `session_01DKWDdUJ2XNRESVVWUvcpnh`), verbatim: 「6335 和以后这种类似的，都立即退休。项目在创业阶段，用户也很少，短期不考虑渐进。」 (6355 by number; 6335 is a typo for this card).

Ruled: **A — retire `timeScale` now.** Tombstone (`?: never` + mirror twin per the #5474 convention), drop the designer input, drop the `resolveTimelineScale` fallback read, drop the docs row — and migrate the two in-repo authors in the same PR (`examples/schema-catalog/.../gantt-style-timeline.json` and the renderer's own `examples.gantt` block). The silent-reversion cost for externally-stored old documents is **accepted by the ruling**: startup stage, very few users. The staged window (option B) is declined.

⭐ **Standing class rule, quoted for future seats**: for this class — a deprecated alias/spelling with the canonical form already ruled — the default is IMMEDIATE retirement, no phased windows, while the project is at startup stage. Recorded into the decision framework via objectstack-ai/objectstack#12668. Sibling #6354's own路线 is unaffected (already immediate).

Dispatch notes: Clause-② per this repo's convention (published-type change ⇒ governed draft, human merge); pin: the old spelling is refused loudly post-change (red-before-fix on a `timeScale`-only document), not silently defaulted.

State: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`.

Claim: `domain:ui` execution seat, session `8ca04858-ea8e-5b85-9182-de59aa49e00c`, branch `claude/issue-6355-retire-timescale-alias`.

The maintainer ruling (2026-08-27) is the order. Four things on top of it.

## ⛔ This PR is NOT mine to enqueue — governed draft, human merge

The ruling's dispatch note is explicit: **Clause-② per this repo's convention (published-type change ⇒ governed draft, human merge).**

So: open it **draft** and **leave it draft**. ⛔ Do not flip ready, do not enable auto-merge, do not enqueue. I will not either — I will report it as ready for a human merge. This differs from every other card this seat has dispatched today, and it differs for a reason: the diff changes a published type.

## The pin is the whole deliverable, and it has a specific shape

> pin: the old spelling is refused **loudly** post-change (red-before-fix on a `timeScale`-only document), not silently defaulted.

The failure this card exists to prevent is a `timeScale`-only document **silently reverting to the default month granularity** — the chart changes and nothing errors. So a test that merely proves `scale` works is not the pin. What must be pinned is that an old-spelling document is **refused**, and it must be shown red before the fix.

⛔ Do not let the tombstone's presence stand in for that. Show the refusal failing on the pre-fix tree, then passing.

## Scope, as the ruling enumerates it — all in ONE PR

- Tombstone `timeScale` (`?: never` **plus the mirror twin**, per the #5474 lockstep convention — both halves or neither).
- Drop the designer input.
- Drop the `resolveTimelineScale` fallback read.
- Drop the docs row.
- **Migrate the two in-repo authors in the same PR**: `examples/schema-catalog/.../gantt-style-timeline.json` and the renderer's own `examples.gantt` block.

Re-verify all five on the current `origin/main` before editing — line and path references in this card predate several merges today.

## On the bump — read this before you reach for `major`

This retires a published alias, so the honest-declaration question arises. **The convention here is `minor` plus the break spelled out in the changeset body** (AGENTS.md §版本号策略): objectui's major is pinned to the `@objectstack` major, and all publishable packages share one `fixed` group. A second dev reached the same reading independently on #6490 today, unprompted.

⛔ If you nonetheless conclude an honest declaration requires `major`, **stop and report — do not fight the gate, and do not re-score to get green.** That exact standoff is live and unresolved on #6366, whose PR is deliberately parked draft-and-red; a second instance of it helps nobody. Reporting is the correct outcome.

## Standing class rule from this ruling, quoted because it governs future cards too

> for this class — a deprecated alias/spelling with the canonical form already ruled — the default is **IMMEDIATE retirement, no phased windows**, while the project is at startup stage.

The staged-window option was declined, and the silent-reversion cost for externally-stored documents is **accepted by the ruling**. So do not re-litigate it, and do not soften the removal into a deprecation warning.

Draft PR, `Fixes #6355`, and leave it draft.

## ACCEPT — PR #6656. ⛔ Stays a DRAFT: this one is HUMAN MERGE.

Reviewed by the `domain:ui` execution seat. Per this card's ruling (published-type change, Clause-②), the PR is **not** flipped ready, **not** enqueued, and has **no** auto-merge. It is finished work waiting on the maintainer.

### Entry qualification

Every check on head `82f289e1`, not the required subset: **29 of 29** returned against `total_count` — 26 `success`, 3 `skipped` (`dependabot`, `Test (coverage)`, `Test (coverage shard …)`), **zero failures, zero still running**. `Type Check` is `completed: success`, and for this change that is not one green among many: **TS2578 makes an unused `@ts-expect-error` an error, so a green type-check is itself the proof the tombstone bites.** A green *test* run would have proved nothing — the directive is type-erased.

### ⭐ The finding that justifies the whole card: deleting the key would have been the bug

The obvious implementation of "retire the alias" is to delete `timeScale`. Measured, that would have been a **silent regression**:

> `BaseSchema` is `.passthrough()` with a `[key: string]: any` index signature — so a **deleted** key still parses and still type-checks green, while the renderer no longer reads it. An author who kept writing `timeScale` would get **no error anywhere** and a silent revert to the `month` default.

That is why the retirement is a **tombstone in lockstep on both halves** — `?: never` on `TimelineSchema` and `z.never().optional()` on the Zod twin — rather than a deletion. This is the same rule this lane has now met three times, in its third face: under an index signature there is no non-membership left to enforce with, so the refusal has to be *declared* rather than inherited from absence.

### ⭐ It found a third author the card did not list — and it was ungreppable

The card named two in-repo authors. There is a third:

> `ObjectTimeline` composes a schema for `TimelineRenderer` and wrote the resolved axis **under the alias**.

That is invisible to any grep of *authored metadata*, because it is not authored — it is code writing the key at runtime. Had the fallback read been dropped without it, **every object-bound gantt would have silently reverted**, and nothing in the corpus would have shown it. Finding it required reading the composition path rather than searching for the spelling.

Writing `scale` after the spread also corrected a **latent precedence inversion**: `timelineConfig.scale` had been losing to a flat `schema.scale` because the resolver read `scale ?? timeScale`. Ablation 3 produced `expected 'day' to be 'year'` — direct evidence, not an inference.

### Shown able to fail, in the strict order

The pin was **committed before its fix** (`ab88df74`) and run on that pre-fix tree — so "red before green" is a property of the history, not a claim. Runtime leg failed on the **refusal assertion specifically** (`a timeScale-only document was ACCEPTED — it will silently revert to the month default`), with its 4 counter-probes passing, so the file failed for the right reason rather than failing wholesale. Compile leg: `tsc` exit 2 with TS2578. Both green after.

The pin asserts the **rejection envelope** (`invalid_type`, `expected: 'never'`, path `timeScale`) rather than merely `success: false` — so it cannot be satisfied by any old refusal.

Three ablations, each with mutation proven on disk (anchored counts on injected **and** removed text, plus a blob-hash delta) and restoration proven **by observation** — blob equal to the HEAD blob **and** `git diff HEAD` clean — never by an exit code. The no-rebuild claim was measured, not assumed: the pins import the mirror relatively and `@object-ui/types/zod` is aliased to source in `vitest.config.mts`, so no dist hop exists on these pairs.

### ⭐ The restore leg caught a defect in the dev's own new pin

Worth keeping, because it is the failure mode that survives a green suite:

> a misplaced `@ts-expect-error` — above the `const` instead of above the property that excess-property checking actually reports on — **suppressed nothing while a real TS2322 stood**.

A directive that guards the wrong line is indistinguishable from a working one until something forces the question. Here the ablation did, and it was fixed and re-ablated rather than noted.

### Two gates reported NOT MEASURED, and were treated as such

`check:doc-snippets` first exited 2 with *"PRECONDITION NOT MET — the snippet program was NOT run"*, and `check:readme-exports` exited 1 with *"the population COLLAPSED — this run proves nothing"* (packagesRead 11 against a floor of 25). Both were recorded as **NOT MEASURED, never as red**, and re-run after building what they name. The green verdicts in the union are from those real runs. A precondition failure read as a pass — or as a failure — would both have been wrong.

The gate set was derived manually from `package.json` + `.github/workflows`, with the reason stated: objectui has no `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`, and objectstack's copy answers only about its own tree. Declaring that beats silently running the wrong tool.

### Scope

All five ruled scope items landed in one PR, each re-verified present on the current `origin/main` before editing. Bump is `minor` with the break spelled out in the changeset body — no major standoff arose. One out-of-scope finding filed as **#6655** (an object-bound timeline with `variant: gantt` throws `RangeError: Invalid time value`), proven **pre-existing** by a byte-identical diff against the merge base rather than assumed to be.

### ⛔ What happens next is the maintainer's

This PR retires a published spelling, so under this card's ruling the merge is a human act and the draft state is the review record. It is green, complete, and waiting. **Nothing further is owed by this seat**, and this seat will not flip, enqueue, or auto-merge it.
